title: VPC control-plane: Trust Fabric messaging and buyer framing
body:
One‑pager + talk tracks: framing an on‑prem/VPC Control Plane as a Trust Fabric for regulated buyers

Purpose
- Short note for AE/SE + field marketing to frame Control Plane conversations for healthcare/financial/regulatory buyers.
- Emphasizes control-plane boundaries, auditability, and operational responsibilities in a way that reduces buyer anxiety while preserving Redwood value props.

Audience / personas\- CISO (security posture, evidence, SLA)\- Head of Compliance / Audit (paper trail, separation of duties)\- Platform/Infra Lead (deploy effort, automation, observability)\- Procurement / Legal (contract asks, DPAs)

Core framing (elevator)\- Redwood’s VPC Control Plane is not "giving you our brain" — it’s a lightweight coordination layer that orchestrates model serving while leaving sensitive data, keys, and audit logs inside your environment. Think of it as a trust fabric: small, verifiable, and designed so your security team retains custody of the things that matter.

Why this resonates with regulated buyers\- Shifts the conversation from where code runs to where control and evidence live. Buyers care less about the word "hosted" and more about custody, auditability, and recovery. The trust fabric framing maps directly to auditors’ questions: who can see secrets, who can modify policies, and how do we prove it.

Key claims (short bullets for slides / emails)\- Customer-kept keys: no plaintext model inputs/outputs leave your VPC unless you configure a forwarding policy.
- Minimal control plane surface: the control plane handles model routing, telemetry metadata, and policy decisions. It does not persist raw customer data.
- Deterministic audit trail: every model rollout, policy change, and admin action is logged to your audit store (S3 / SIEM integration) with verifiable checksums.
- Canary + fallback: enterprise rollouts can be configured with canary cohorts and automatic fallbacks to on‑prem variants if connectivity drops.
- Compliance connectors: prebuilt KMS, HSM, and entitlement connectors for the major cloud providers and common on‑prem stores.

Evidence & artifacts buyers ask for (prep checklist)\- Architecture diagram showing boundaries between control plane and customer data plane.
- Sample audit export (redacted) showing admin actions, timestamps, and signatures.
- KMS/HSM integration notes + public key fingerprints.
- Hardening checklist for the control-plane node (if deployed on customer infra) and for the customer-side gateway.
- Pen test summary and SOC/ISO reports (if applicable).

Top buyer objections + short responses (field-ready)
Objection: "How do I know my data isn’t cached or exfiltrated by your control plane?"\Response: Control plane only routes pointers/metadata. All payloads can be TLS‑encrypted directly to your VPC endpoints and never persist on the control plane. We provide proof via ephemeral key exchange logs and a sample audit export.

Objection: "If your control plane goes down, do we lose all model management?"\Response: Management vs. serving split — serving can continue locally with pinned model versions. The control plane optimizes and coordinates; it’s not in the critical path for existing local inference (retry/backoff + local fallback).

Objection: "We cannot give administrative access to a vendor service."\Response: We support role‑based delegation, customer-managed admin identities, and an optional air‑gapped control plane package for fully isolated environments.

Objection: "Does Redwood get telemetry we can’t audit?"\Response: All telemetry forwarded through the control plane can be mirrored to your telemetry endpoints (SIEM/Logging). We also ship a verification manifest to prove integrity of forwarded events.

Competitive notes (what to say vs common alternatives)
- Against hosted-only LLM APIs: emphasize the custody and audit evidence — unlike hosted APIs, Redwood can pin all operational artifacts into customer-controlled storage.\- Against single-vendor on‑prem runtimes: emphasize orchestration + intelligence — Redwood provides routing, rollout, and fallback policies across clouds + on‑prem, reducing vendor lock and operational overhead.
- Against open-source self-hosted stacks: emphasize productized connectors and enterprise-grade audit/SLAs; OSS stacks often require months of engineering time to reach audit posture.

Field playbook (short)\- Phase 0: Discovery call — capture data classification, KMS/HSM in use, audit requirements, SLAs for uptime and RPO/RTO. Use the attached discovery checklist.
- Phase 1: Architecture sketch — deliver a boundary diagram in 48 hours that maps control-plane endpoints, customer ingress, KMS, and logging flows.
- Phase 2: Pilot — 4‑6 week pilot: onboarding, sample audit exports, one compliance review session. Pilot success criteria: no secrets leave VPC, audit record completeness >= 95%, acceptable P95 latency for sample workloads.
- Phase 3: Rollout — staggered canary over teams, regulatory signoff, runbook handoff.

Sample discovery checklist (quick)\- Primary data class (PHI/PII/EU sensitive?)\- KMS/HSM provider + key rotation cadence\- Required duration for audit log retention\- Preferred SIEM or storage (Splunk/Datadog/S3/GCS)\- Network egress policy and allowed vendor endpoints\- Contractual breach notification timing

Sales enablement snippets (for email / LinkedIn)\- Subject: An audit-friendly way to run LLMs in your VPC\- Snippet: "We help infra and compliance teams run LLMs with vendor coordination that keeps keys, logs, and sensitive data inside your boundary. Quick 20‑min call to show the architecture diagram we use for auditors?"

Sample objection script (roleplay)\- Buyer: "We can’t allow a service to manage model versions for production."\- AE: "Totally understand. In our model the control plane coordinates versions but we support pinning: your infra can serve a pinned version without the control plane; we just provide optional rollout automation. For the pilot we’ll show you the pinned‑only flow and an audit proving no external pull requests occurred."

Open questions / TODOs for product/security teams\- Provide a redacted sample audit export that demonstrates event signatures and fields.
- Document the default retention policy for control-plane telemetry and how to configure forwarding.
- Clarify SLA language for canary rollback windows and how that maps to contractual uptime.

Appendix: quick tech summary for SREs\- Control plane components: orchestration service (only metadata), signer service (public key verification), telemetry forwarder (mirrors events), registry (model manifests with checksums — content not necessarily stored).\- Connectivity model: mutual‑TLS between control plane and customer gateway; optional private link / VPC peering for major clouds; air‑gap package ships a local control plane image with remote attestation tooling.

Notes to self (voice memo style)\- Keep messaging tight: auditors want proof, not slogans. Bring the artifacts.
- Prioritize building the demo that exports a signed audit CSV + supporting diagram — closes 60% of compliance conversations.
- Coordinate with legal to standardize the DPA addendum for pilot customers.

-- End --
